correctness.rationale: Strong lumpability gives the exact three-state tilted count matrix with same-orbit transitions retained. The stationary mean and mean-zero Poisson corrector reproduce the rational Fano law; the independent determinant calculation agrees symbolically. Difference factorizations establish positivity and strict growth for every integer m>=2. A fast-hub variation-of-constants and uniform finite-horizon Gronwall argument proves convergence of fixed-time MGFs to independent rate-two Poisson singletons and doublets. Independent full-configuration numerical calculations match the exact Fano law for m=1 through m=12; m=1 is only a consistency boundary. Finite tests are corroborative, not proof.

value.rationale: The two-particle activity count is a standard, physically motivated observable. This exact infinite-family classification quantifies a nontrivial fluctuation effect unseen by the qualitative finite-network Poisson criterion: F increases strictly from 29/25 to 5/3 even as particle density tends to zero. The fixed-time compound-Poisson limit explains the persistent excess by fast hub-induced double jumps while peripheral edges produce singleton jumps. The precise invariant is tied to this hub-and-blade transport mechanism, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
